title: A Room for the Harvest
premise: August Villalobos takes a teaching post at Hollow Creek School, where students vanish from their desks mid-lesson and the staff's cheerful denials grow more rehearsed by the day. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the old well, August discovers the school was built as a feeding pen for something invited in generations ago — and his predecessor left records naming him as the next 'keeper.' To survive until sunrise, August must choose between burning the truth that would free the town and preserving the loyalty of the one colleague who believes him, ending with him sealing himself inside the door so the harvest ends with him.
about_author: E. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who taught for eleven years in towns too small to appear on maps, collecting the stories colleagues only told after dark. Delacroix now writes full-time from a farmhouse whose cellar door has been locked since before they moved in.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: August's POV. His first week at Hollow Creek: roll call lists names of children no one has seen in months, yet their parents send lunch money. Vice Principal Marisol Vega deflects every question with practiced warmth. The emotional beat is creeping wrongness — August's rationalism holding, but barely, as he finds his predecessor's lesson plans still on the chalkboard, dated three years ahead.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Well
chapters.summary: August's POV, shifting to Marisol's midway through. The excavation crew breaks ground for a new wing and unearths an iron door scratched shut from within; that night, two crew members are found standing in the parking lot, smiling, unable to say their own names. Marisol finally confesses the school's covenant. The beat is dread giving way to complicity — she begs him not to dig further.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She leads August into the sub-basement and shows him the ledger: every keeper since 1911, each one a teacher who chose the town over the truth. The thing behind the door offers August his missing students, alive, if he accepts the role. The climax arrives as he nearly signs — then recognizes his predecessor's handwriting in his own journal entries. The beat is temptation curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Until Sunrise
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging on August alone below. He burns the ledger, severing the covenant, but the door must be held shut from inside until sunrise or everything taken returns wrong. Marisol holds the rope above him, weeping, loyal at last to truth over town. As dawn light seeps through the well shaft, August speaks the students' names aloud — remembering them — and the door goes quiet. The beat is sacrifice transfigured into witness.
